clue.text: Generating good manners

definitions.meaning: producing offspring, as in raising animals

explanation.definitionFit: Both the act of producing young and the polish of a well-raised person go by this one word.

clue.text: Doctor spotted personal hygiene issue requiring three directions

parts.note: spotted means saw, past tense of see
BO is body odour
N, E and S are the compass points north, east and south

explanation.surface: A doctor notices a patient's smell and needs to be pointed three ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for a surgeon or doctor, from the old days of amputation.

clue.text: Why one is attending sale that's uninviting

parts.note: what for? asks why, so the purpose word is for
bidding is what someone does at an auction sale

explanation.surface: Asks the reason a person goes to an auction, which proves unwelcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Why one is attending sale' as the answer 'for bidding': the reason to go to an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a grim, forbidding look is off-putting and unwelcoming.

clue.text: Gambling game played very loudly in the distance

parts.note: faro is an old card game played for stakes
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A card game is played noisily somewhere far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something remote or distant lies far away.

clue.text: Way leading character enters bar

indicators.note: enters says one piece goes inside the bar word

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
A leads the alphabet

explanation.surface: A star actor walks into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading character' suggests a star, but it is A, first of the alphabet; 'bar' is a rod, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a road is a route or way.

clue.text: Temperature line more confused with this

indicators.note: confused means the letters of more and this are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A forecaster's temperature chart grows more muddled with this.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, a line joining places with equal temperature is called by this name.

clue.text: Gather Scottish course is detaining French duke

indicators.note: detaining means holding, so the river word holds the duke inside

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, a watercourse
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: A Scottish golf course holds a French aristocrat in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests golf, but it is a river's course: the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to gather or infer something is to conclude it from evidence.

clue.text: Dope comes from north with endless abundance

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for abundance is dropped

parts.note: oodles means lots, an abundance

explanation.surface: Drugs arrive from the north in plentiful supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' hints at drugs, but here it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a noodle is a silly person, a dope or fool.

clue.text: A jolly lady that sailed from Spain

parts.note: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful woman who set sail from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada was the fleet that sailed from Spain against England in 1588.

clue.text: One fine piece of work, and just as well

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a well done task, and idiomatically a British phrase meaning it is lucky that.

clue.text: Transfusion of fresh talent?

parts.note: a transfusion literally gives a patient someone else's blood, and fresh recruits are figuratively this

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for recruits bringing fresh energy to a team, pictured here as a medical transfusion.

clue.text: Found in shack: left-handed comb

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A left-handed comb turns up inside a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel comb used to dress flax or hemp fibres goes by this name.

clue.text: Sort out a profit — one grand, possibly

indicators.note: sort out means the letters of a profit one are rearranged

explanation.surface: Settle a profit worth a thousand pounds, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one grand' looks like a thousand pounds, but a grand is a grand piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is one kind of piano, so the full instrument name is defined by example.

clue.text: Catch final stage of race?

definitions.meaning: to arrest someone, informal 'the police ran him in'
the last stretch approaching the finish

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to arrest; as a noun it is the approach to the finishing line.

clue.text: Grand, having immensity of good food

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
something astronomical is immense in size

explanation.surface: A grand feast of enormous size.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant of gastronomic: relating to fine eating and cookery.

clue.text: Quantity of hay and old wood in carriage

parts.note: a rick is a stack of hay
shaw is an archaic word for a thicket or small wood

explanation.surface: Hay and old timber are loaded into a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person is a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Being in credit, getting article with initial deduction

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: initial deduction means the first letter of the article word is taken off

parts.note: a feature is an article in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone in credit gets a newspaper piece after a deduction at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a grammar word (a, the) but is a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a living being or animal is a creature.

clue.text: Relax, I will take father something sweet

parts.note: to loll is to lounge lazily
pop is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A child says relax, I'll take Dad along to buy a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sweet on a stick is an example of a sweet treat.

clue.text: Arrive at a time volunteers may get in

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers are told when they can arrive to be let in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to attain a goal is to reach or arrive at it.

clue.text: This writer needs a rest from South African corn

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
to lie is to rest, as a lie-down

explanation.surface: An author needs a break from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: In South African English, maize is called by this name.

clue.text: Novel recalled in pantomime

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of recalled in are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A book remembered within a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the anagram signal; pantomime is the British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: The rags-to-riches fairy tale is one of the best known British Christmas pantomimes.

clue.text: Moving job with an order muddled up? Nothing's missing

indicators.note: muddled up means the letters of an order are jumbled
missing says the round letter for nothing is left out

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A removal job with a muddled order, but nothing has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes the O (nothing) from AN ORDER, and 'muddled up' scrambles the remaining ANRDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip run to do a task, a job that involves going somewhere.

clue.text: Line of fat — or lean — right inside meat

indicators.note: inside says one letter goes within the meat word

parts.note: steak is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: A butcher describes a cut with right in the middle, fat or lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a band or stripe, as in the bands of fat and lean in streaky bacon.

clue.text: Immediate treatment needed to make tree steady

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
staid means steady, sober

explanation.surface: Treatment is needed at once to keep a tree upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency medical help given on the spot before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Pair of braces

parts.note: a brace is a pair, so two braces make two pairs

explanation.definitionFit: A brace is two of something, so two braces total this number.

clue.text: After said dancing who reported commotion?

indicators.note: said means the dance word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: ballet is a form of dancing

indicators.note: reported means who is heard spoken

parts.note: taken as written, then heard

explanation.surface: Someone asks who was dancing, and there was uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ballyhoo is a noisy fuss or hubbub.

clue.text: Thin point on weapon

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass
an arrow is shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A slender tip on a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something narrow is slim or thin.

clue.text: Criminals' environment in life and death?

definitions.text: Criminals' environment in life and death?

parts.words: Criminals' environment in life and death?
parts.note: gangland is where criminals live, and the realm of the dead is where all go after dying

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both organised crime's milieu and the mythological realm of the dead, like Hades.
